item.title: Home minister: Govt advancing plans to harness Blue Economy potential
item.description:
Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed on Friday said the government is moving forward with various plans to harness the potential of the Blue Economy.
“The country will be able to generate substantial revenue if its marine resources and seaports are being utilized properly and the government is progressing plans to rein the potentials of our Blue Economy,” he said
He made the remark while addressing the inaugural ceremony of the Cox's Bazar Development Authority (CDA) Residential Flat Development Project-1 as the chief guest in Cox's Bazar.
He said the government is working to further enrich the tourism industry in Cox's Bazar and elevate it to international standards.
“Country's economy could benefit significantly by fully realizing the district's immense tourism potential,” he added.
"Tourism cannot be limited to the construction of high-rise buildings alone," stressing the nature preservation, he said.
He added that activities should be spread across the entire 100-kilometre stretch of Cox's Bazar Sea beach.
He stressed the need to promote the beauty of Cox's Bazar globally to attract travelers.
He also said the government has planned to establish a Marine University to expand opportunities for higher education and marine research centered on Cox's Bazar.
“Once implemented, the initiative will open a new horizon for marine education, research and the development of skilled human resources,” he added.
Later, Salahuddin laid the foundation stone of the new building of the 500-bed Cox's Bazar Medical College Hospital.
Lawmaker Shahjahan Chowdhury of the Ukhiya-Teknaf constituency, Alamgir Mohammad Mahfuzullah Farid of the Maheshkhali-Kutubdia constituency, and reserved seat lawmaker Shamima Ara Swapna, Deputy Commissioner Abdul Mannan, Superintendent of Police ANM Sajedur Rahman, Chairman of the Cox's Bazar Development Authority and representatives of various government departments were present on the occasion.

item.title: Aminul: Shakib has no scope to return to Bangladesh now
item.description:
State Minister for Sports Aminul Haque has said Shakib Al Hasan no longer has any scope to return to Bangladesh through the normal process, citing the former all-rounder’s current political position.
“ [Shakib] has completely taken a position as a politician. The person who is with the autocrat, I do not think there is any opportunity for him to come anymore,” Aminul told Bangla Tribune on Friday.
He made the remarks after Reuters published an interview with Shakib, in which the former Bangladesh cricketer said he had not received any cooperation from the current government regarding his return to the country.
Aminul, however, rejected the allegation of non-cooperation, saying the government had previously been willing to take a flexible approach to Shakib’s case if he wanted to return to Bangladesh to play cricket.
“We were flexible regarding Shakib Al Hasan. If he had come to the country to play, we would have been flexible with him and looked into everything. That was how we were viewing the matter. But in the current situation, that is no longer possible,” he said.
Regarding Shakib’s allegation of non-cooperation, Aminul said he had repeatedly stated that the matter would be handled with flexibility.
“There is nothing of non-cooperation here. I have repeatedly said that Shakib’s matter would be viewed flexibly. I myself spoke with the home minister so that the legal processes could proceed flexibly. Even after that, I did not see any non-cooperation,” he said.
“Besides, Shakib did not return to the country and enter into a legal battle,” the state minister added.
Aminul said the government had been considering Shakib’s return primarily from the perspective of his role as a cricketer.
“As a player, which is what we were considering, we were flexible. We were viewing it that way. Now there is no opportunity for flexibility anymore,” he said.
The state minister said Shakib would have to pursue a legal course if he decides to return to Bangladesh under the current circumstances.
“If he comes, then he will have to fight legally,” Aminul said.

item.title: Police warn of coordinated smear campaign targeting key officials
item.description:
Bangladesh Police Headquarters on Friday warned of a coordinated smear campaign on Facebook and other social media platforms targeting senior police officials and key government figures, urging the public not to believe or spread rumours.
In a press release, the Police Headquarters said a "vested quarter" has been disseminating fabricated, misleading and provocative content to create public confusion.
It alleged that "the ousted fascist forces and their local and foreign allies" were behind the campaign to destabilise law and order, undermine police morale and tarnish the government's image.
According to the statement, the propaganda intensified after Bangladesh Police launched strict legal action against banned political organisations and refused what it described as "unlawful lobbying" by those involved.
The Police Headquarters also claimed to have evidence that some individuals behind the campaign are accused in various criminal cases, attempted to influence police and other government agencies, and demanded money in exchange for refraining from spreading defamatory content.
Urging citizens to act responsibly, the police called on the public not to believe, share or circulate misleading and provocative posts on social media, stressing the need to prevent rumours and disinformation.
It warned that anyone found involved in such propaganda would face strict legal action under existing laws.
Reaffirming its commitment to maintaining law and order, the Police Headquarters said Bangladesh Police would continue to perform its duties with professionalism, dedication and public cooperation, while seeking greater public vigilance against disinformation campaigns.

item.title: Where hills, forests and lakes make the perfect one-day escape
item.description:
There are places where a short journey is enough to leave the noise and rush of city life behind. Madhutila Eco Park in Sherpur is one such destination — a place where green hills, dense forests, quiet trails and a lake come together to offer a refreshing retreat in the lap of nature.
Set against the foothills of the Garo Hills, the park offers a chance to breathe in fresh air, walk through greenery and spend a leisurely day surrounded by the calm of the natural landscape.
Madhutila Eco Park is located in the border-adjacent area of Nalitabari upazila in Sherpur district. Built at the foothills of the Garo Hills, the park blends the charm of the hills with the atmosphere of a forest.
The moment visitors enter, the scenery begins to change. Green trees stretch along the pathways, while the undulating hills and quiet surroundings create a welcome contrast to the bustle of urban life.
For families, the park offers a setting for a picnic; for friends, a place to gather and unwind; and for those travelling alone, an opportunity to simply slow down and spend some time with nature.
The hills are among Madhutila's biggest attractions. From elevated points, visitors can look out over the surrounding greenery and take in the landscape from a different perspective.
The park also features an artificial lake where visitors can enjoy boating. Children have access to various entertainment facilities, while those who prefer a quieter experience can walk through the forest and explore its natural surroundings.
For photography enthusiasts, almost every turn offers a potential frame — from the green-covered hills and trees to the lake and winding paths.
Nature lovers, in particular, can find plenty to appreciate in the combination of forest, hills and open spaces.
The journey to Madhutila begins with a trip from Dhaka to Sherpur. Visitors can travel by bus to Sherpur city and then head towards Nalitabari upazila.
From Nalitabari, local transport can take visitors directly to Madhutila Eco Park.
Those travelling by private car can use the Dhaka-Mymensingh-Sherpur road. The journey itself becomes part of the experience, with rural landscapes and stretches of green scenery unfolding along the way.
A day at Madhutila does not necessarily require a large budget. The total cost will depend on the choice of transport and the distance travelled.
The main expenses include transportation from Dhaka to Sherpur, local transport between Sherpur and the park, as well as food and other personal expenses.
Travelling with friends or family can make the trip more affordable, as transportation and other expenses can be shared among the group.
Winter is arguably the most comfortable time to explore Madhutila Eco Park. With pleasant weather, visitors can spend more time walking along the hilly trails, exploring the forest and enjoying the scenery without the discomfort of excessive heat.
But the park has a different charm after the monsoon. The hills and forests become intensely green, giving the landscape a fresh and vibrant appearance.
Whether it is the cool calm of winter or the lush greenery following the rains, each season offers its own way of experiencing Madhutila.
Not every escape needs to involve a long holiday or an elaborate itinerary. Sometimes, all it takes is a road leading away from the city, a stretch of green hills and a few quiet hours outdoors.
With its forests, hills, lake and peaceful surroundings, Madhutila Eco Park offers exactly that — a chance to step away from the city's hurried rhythm and reconnect with nature, even if only for a day.
And when the journey home begins, the quiet landscapes of Sherpur may linger in the mind a little longer, turning a simple day trip into a memory worth keeping.

item.title: Golam Parwar accuses India of diplomatic breach over Hasina press meet
item.description:
Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami Secretary General and former MP Mia Golam Parwar on Friday accused India of violating diplomatic norms by allowing deposed former prime minister Sheikh Hasina to hold a press conference in New Delhi while continuing to shelter her.
His remarks came in a statement issued by the party's central publicity department, which also strongly condemned India's actions.
Parwar said Bangladesh is committed to maintaining mutually respectful diplomatic relations with India and all other countries based on equality, while upholding the sovereignty and independence of every nation.
He alleged that India had ignored repeated diplomatic requests from Bangladesh to return sheikh Hasina and, instead, continued to provide her shelter and a platform to engage in activities he claimed were directed against Bangladesh.
Parwar alleged that the government led by Sheikh Hasina had subjected Bangladeshis to widespread repression, including killings and enforced disappearances, during its more than 16 years in power. He further claimed that the government carried out a "genocide" during the July-August 2024 mass uprising, in which around 1,500 people were killed and more than 30,000 injured. He said these figures had been documented by national and international media, the United Nations fact-finding mission and various human rights organisations.
He further claimed that the interim government had repeatedly sought Hasina's extradition through official communications, but India had not responded positively. He alleged that by continuing to shelter her, India appeared to be supporting the Awami League rather than respecting Bangladesh's requests and the existing bilateral prisoner exchange agreement.
Parwar urged the Indian government to reconsider its position and hand over Hasina to the Bangladeshi authorities.
He also criticised the government for failing to bring Hasina back despite the second anniversary of the July mass uprising, saying the delay had allowed her to continue making statements from abroad.
Calling for stronger diplomatic efforts, Parwar urged the government to pursue an Interpol Red Notice and seek United Nations support to facilitate Hasina's return. He warned that the government would face public scrutiny if it failed to take effective measures.
He also called on the public to remain united and vigilant against what he described as attempts by "fascist forces" to re-emerge, urging citizens to work towards building a united, just, corruption-free and secure Bangladesh.

item.title: Three Narayanganj gas leak explosion victims remain critical
item.description:
Three members of the same family, including an eight-year-old child, remain in critical condition after suffering severe burn injuries in an explosion caused by a gas leak in Narayanganj early Friday.
The injured — Md Maidul Islam, 27, Mosha Beauty Akter, 24, and Md Maruf, 8 — are undergoing treatment at the National Institute of Burn and Plastic Surgery.
They were admitted to the hospital’s emergency department at around 9am.
Residential Physician Dr Shawon Bin Rahman said the three were brought to the hospital following an explosion caused by a gas line leak in the Narayanganj area.
“Maidul sustained burns to 85% of his body, Beauty sustained burns to 80%, and Maruf sustained burns to 90%,” he said.
“All three patients are in critical condition,” he added.

item.title: Shama Obaed: Govt working to curb syndicates exploiting students looking to study abroad
item.description:
State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam on Friday said the government is working to curb unscrupulous syndicates and brokers who exploit Bangladeshi students seeking to pursue higher education abroad by charging them excessive money.
“Unscrupulous syndicates or brokers take advantage of our students, who have to pay extremely high amounts of money to go abroad. The government is obviously aware of the issue and is working on it,” she said.
The state minister said while addressing the inaugural session of the two-day 14th International Education Expo 2026, organized by the Foreign Admission and Career Development Consultants Association of Bangladesh (FACD-CAB), at a city hotel.
This year the fair brought together representatives from 30 countries to provide consultancy services for around 300 world-class educational institutions around the world.
Shama Obaed said the foreign ministry has already opened a migration wing for the first time to address the migration related problems. The sole responsibility of this newly opened wing is to address all sorts of migration related problems.
She urged FACD-CAB and others concerned to help the wing by providing necessary information to contain the unscrupulous syndicates in the student migration process.
“Together, we have to work in a unison way here. We have to work together to bring these broker syndicates under the law. They are unfairly destroying the future of our children (students),” she said.
The state minister said the foreign ministry is ready to cooperate with FACD-CAB to make the migration process more transparent and accountable and to help it provide better services to Bangladeshi students.
She asked FACD-CAB to submit in writing its demands and problems so that the issues could be brought to the attention of the Prime Minister as well as the Foreign Ministry together with other concerned ministries, including the Education, Finance and Home ministries, could fulfill their demands and address the problems.
Shama Obaed stressed the importance of creating a safe and investment-friendly environment in Bangladesh so that students attained overseas education and experiences can return home and contribute to the country's development.
“We certainly want our children to go abroad and study. But at the same time, we need to create a safe, investment-friendly and secure environment in Bangladesh where they can return, invest and become entrepreneurs and thus help the government build the country,” she said.
Describing education as an important instrument of diplomacy, she said the Ministry of Foreign Affairs will continue to encourage educational and research partnerships between Bangladesh and other countries.
Bangladesh's missions abroad can help connect Bangladeshi institutions with international universities, facilitate academic cooperation and support the legitimate interests and welfare of Bangladeshi students.
Referring to the national budget for 2026-2027 fiscal year, the state minister said the government has given the highest-ever allocation to the education sector in the latest budget, reflecting its priority to education.
The International Education fair, a flagship international education event, started at Pan Pacific Sonargaon Hotel, bringing together education consultants, international university representatives, students, and stakeholders under one platform.
Visitors need prior registration to visit the education fair from 10:00am to 8:00pm.
Visitors get scope to interact directly with representatives of universities from different countries and receive guidance on scholarships, financial aid, tuition fees, visa processing and career planning.

item.title: Mir Helal: July Uprising belongs to people, not any group
item.description:
State Minister for Land and Chittagong Hill Tracts Affairs, Barrister Mir Mohammed Helal Uddin, said it is both inaccurate and misleading to portray the July-August 2024 mass uprising as the achievement of any single individual or group.
"No one can claim ownership of this mass uprising. It belongs to the 18 crore people of Bangladesh," he said.
He said the true outcome of the mass uprising was realized when the people resolved that they would no longer tolerate oppression and that the authoritarian government had to be removed.
He made the remarks while addressing a discussion titled "Fascism, July Revolution and Today's Bangladesh" as the chief guest at the July Memorial Hall of the Chittagong Press Club on Friday afternoon.
The discussion was jointly organized by the Chittagong Press Club and the Chittagong Metropolitan Union of Journalists (CMUJ).
City BNP Convener Ershad Ullah, MP, and Abu Sufian, MP, among others, addressed the event as special guests.
He said Bangladesh had been heavily burdened by the Awami League's 15 years of misrule, during which BNP leaders and activists were subjected to enforced disappearances, severe torture, and false cases.
He added that people from various professions, including journalists with dissenting views, also faced repression, ultimately leading to the July-August mass uprising as a response to years of oppression.
Mir Helal said the uprising was not intended to bring anyone to state power or government; rather, it was fought to establish Bangladesh as a truly independent and sovereign nation.
Zahidul Karim Kachi, president of the Chittagong Press Club, delivered the welcome address. The discussion was moderated by the club's General Secretary Golam Mawla Murad and Joint Secretary Meah Mohammed Arif.
CMUJ President Mohammad Shah Nawaz presided over the event.
Among others, Chittagong University Vice Chancellor Dr Mohammad Al-Forkan, Premier University Vice Chancellor Prof Dr Nasrul Quadir, Chittagong Development Authority Chairman Engineer Belayet Hossain, Chittagong City BNP Joint Convener MA Aziz, Chittagong District Bar Association President Advocate Tarique Ahmed, Press Club Vice President Mustafa Nayyem, Chittagong Metropolitan Union of Journalists General Secretary Saleh Noman, and Advocate Abdus Sattar, an injured July uprising participant and former president of the Chittagong District Bar Association, also spoke at the program.

item.title: UGC brings major reforms to research proposal evaluation
item.description:
Bangladesh University Grants Commission (UGC) has introduced significant reforms to the evaluation process for research project proposals to ensure greater transparency, impartiality, and accountability in research funding.
These necessary changes have been made at every stage of proposal preparation, submission and evaluation in the research sub-project selection process under the second phase of the Higher Education Acceleration and Transformation (HEAT) project, said a press release here.
Under the new system, proposals submitted for research funding are being evaluated through special codes while keeping the identity of the applicant researcher and their affiliated institution concealed.
Additionally, final reviewers are being selected through a lottery from a panel of potential reviewers, eliminating any scope for personal identification or institutional influence.
UGC Chairman Prof Dr Mamun Ahmed shared this information on Friday as the chief guest at a workshop titled "Introduction to Sub-Project Evaluation" organized under the HEAT project at the Bangladesh Academy of Sciences in the city.
The UGC Chairman said that some negative perceptions had developed surrounding sub-project selection in the first phase of the HEAT project.
Although those perceptions differed from reality, UGC does not want any kind of negative impression to persist among researchers and the academic community. For this reason, maximum importance has been given to transparency and impartiality in the evaluation process of the second phase.
He also informed that after forming an initial reviewer panel from three reliable sources, a high-level committee determined the final panel by verifying the relevant researchers' publications, research experience, and capabilities. Two reviewers have been selected through a lottery for each proposal.
He further said that the 180 research projects that received funding last year are being regularly monitored. If any irregularities or failures to achieve set targets are found in any project, funding will be stopped and legal action will be taken.

item.title: Bobby Hajjaj: Youth to be prepared with proper skills before going to Japan
item.description:
State Minister for Primary and Mass Education, Bobby Hajjaj on Friday said Bangladeshi youths will be prepared according to international standards through language education, technical skills and technological knowledge considering the demands of the international labor market, including Japan.
He said the government's goal is not only to send manpower abroad, but also to develop skilled, language-proficient and world-class human resources.
The state minister made the remarks at a view-exchange meeting with Bangladeshi students, professionals and community representatives living in Osaka and Kobe at a local community center in Osaka, Japan.
"Bangladesh's youths are our greatest strength. The government is continuously working to develop them with international-standard language education, technical skills and technological capabilities," he said.
If skilled manpower can be created according to the demands of the labor market of developed countries like Japan, it will make an important contribution to the country's economy, employment and foreign earnings," Bobby Hajjaj added.
He said necessary policy and institutional initiatives will be taken to further strengthen language education, skill development and quality technical education.
The experiences and recommendations of expatriate Bangladeshis will be considered with importance through coordination with the relevant ministries and agencies, he continued.
Assuring that the issue of ensuring that no talented student misses the opportunity for higher education abroad only due to financial constraints will be given due importance, Bobby Hajjaj said Bangladeshi students studying abroad are important assets for the country.
Their experiences and practical suggestions will play an important role in formulating future policies on education, skill development and human resource formation, he said.
Participants at the meeting emphasized improving the quality of Japanese language education in Bangladesh, introducing a national accreditation system for language education institutions and establishing specialized training institutes for language teachers.
They also called for integrating technical and vocational education and training (TVET) with information technology education.
They also proposed policy support to utilize the skills acquired by young people returning home after training in Japan in the engineering, technology and automotive industries.
Responding to the recommendations, the state minister said the government would work with importance to improve the quality of Japanese language education, formulate a quality control system, enhance teachers' skills and expand technical education suitable for the international labor market.
He also said policy support would be ensured to utilize the knowledge acquired by returning expatriates in the country's industrial and production sectors.
Officials from the Bangladesh Embassy in Tokyo, Bangladeshi students studying at different universities in Japan, expatriate professionals, businesspeople and community leaders attended the exchange meeting.

item.title: Why Iran is sending mixed signals on talks
item.description:
US President Donald Trump on Monday said that negotiations with Iran were ongoing over the Strait of Hormuz, adding that the Islamic Republic was facing a “last chance before decapitation.”
Trump told reporters at the White House that he agreed to continue to pursue talks with Iran at the request of Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Qatar and other countries.
His remarks appeared to contradict public statements from Tehran, which has so far denied that negotiations with Washington were taking place.
Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei nevertheless confirmed that Tehran was holding talks with Oman over the strategic waterway.
The two sides may therefore be describing the same diplomatic channel in different terms, each using language aimed at its own domestic audience.
Washington describes the Omani mediation as negotiations with Iran. Tehran portrays it as a technical discussion with Oman about shipping through the strait.
The Strait of Hormuz has become the main sticking point.
Commercial traffic through key waterway remains severely restricted, while ships continue to face attacks near the strait.
According to data from maritime analytics company Kpler cited by Reuters news agency, only six commercial vessels crossed the route on Monday, down from seven the previous day.
The uncertainty surrounding the key waterway has also affected global markets.
Hopes of diplomatic progress recently pushed oil prices lower and helped stock markets rise. But those movements reflected how sensitive markets remain to any news about the strait, rather than evidence that the crisis had been resolved.
Iran wants some measure of control over vessels entering the Persian Gulf to be recognized. The United States wants the strait fully reopened to unrestricted international shipping.
Babak Dorbeiki, a London-based political analyst and former official at Iran’s Strategic Research Center, told DW that the disagreement is no longer simply about whether the two sides are talking.
“The question is what to call those talks and what each side hopes to gain from them,” he said.
Trump describes the indirect channel as negotiations because he needs to show that military and economic pressure has brought Tehran back to the table, Dorbeiki said.
He suggested that Iran avoids the same terminology because acknowledging negotiations with Washington could be seen by its domestic opponents as surrender.
The two sides remain far apart.
“Iran wants control over vessels entering the strait, while the United States wants completely free passage,” Dorbeiki said. “These positions cannot easily be reconciled.”
The contradictory messages also reflect divisions between rival political factions inside Iran.
Dorbeiki identifies two broad camps.
“The first, which could be described as the ‘development and reconstruction through agreement’ camp, believes that without sanctions relief and the reopening of Hormuz, Iran’s economy cannot recover or even sustain itself,” he told DW.
According to Dorbeiki, Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf and some Revolutionary Guard figures with economic interests may be closer to that view.
The opposing camp, which includes the Paydari Front, a small, ultra-conservative party, “sees an agreement with the United States as an ideological defeat” and favors continued resistance.
The lack of a clear leader in Iran has added to the uncertainty.
Since the country’s then-supreme leader Ali Khamenei was killed in an airstrike on February 28 the first hours of the US-Israeli war against Iran, authority has become more fragmented.
His son Mojtaba Khamenei was named new supreme leader, but his role remains unclear and he has not been seen in public since the war began amid speculation he was severely injured in the strike.
Dorbeiki says this has allowed rival groups to claim they speak for the leadership.
“Indirect talks through Oman are likely to continue,” he told DW. “Pezeshkian will remain under pressure, but he is unlikely to be removed for now because the domestic and international political costs would be high.”
Dorbeiki noted that keeping Pezeshkian in office leaves open the option of blaming him if the negotiations fail.
Hassan Asadi Zeidabadi, an Iranian political analyst based in Tehran, believes the main decision-makers in Tehran have already accepted the need for negotiations.
However, he says there are three main camps within the Iranian establishment.
The first consists of government officials dealing with the economic effects of the war and blockade, making them more inclined toward negotiations.
“The second group is made up mainly of military figures who want to improve their position in the conflict before negotiating and remain skeptical of US intentions,” Zeidabadi told DW.
“The third group is made up of ideological hardliners who believe that reaching an agreement with Washington after the war and the killing of Iran’s supreme leader would mark the end of the Islamic Republic’s traditional identity, which is rooted in opposition to the West.”
“They fear the day after an agreement,” Asadi Zeidabadi added. “For them, a deal with the United States would mean the end of the ideological era they represent and, ultimately, their own removal.”Zeidabadi said these hardliners retain influence in parliament, the security establishment and the state’s propaganda apparatus, and fear the changes a deal could bring.
The future of the talks may depend less on Muscat or Washington than on which factions gain the upper hand in Tehran.
If supporters of an agreement convince the leadership that continued isolation threatens reconstruction, the economy and ultimately the system’s survival, diplomacy could move forward.
If hardliners succeed in presenting any compromise as surrender, even the indirect talks could collapse.
Based on the positions outlined by both analysts, further reports of progress are likely to be accompanied by contradictory public statements.

item.title: Meta ordered to pay US state $567m to abate ‘public nuisance’ and child harm
item.description:
A New Mexico judge on Thursday ordered Meta to pay more than half a billion dollars over the state’s claims that the social media giant created a “public nuisance” and harmed children.
Meta was previously ordered to pay $375 million in damages to New Mexico in March when a jury found the company liable for endangering children by making them vulnerable to predators on its platforms, among other harms.
“We disagree with the ruling and will appeal,” Meta told AFP in a statement Thursday.
“We work hard to keep people safe on our platforms and have been transparent about the challenges of identifying and removing bad actors and harmful content,” the tech giant added.
New Mexico Attorney General Raul Torrez sued Meta -- which makes Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp -- in 2023, alleging the company failed to protect children from online dangers.
During closing arguments, prosecutor Linda Singer told jurors that Meta’s algorithms had directed adults toward content posted by teenage users while the company concealed internal findings about the risks to young people.
In March, the jury found Meta violated the state’s Unfair Practices Act by misleading consumers about the safety of its products for children.
“This case has always been about protecting children, standing up for families, and making sure that one of the world’s largest technology companies cannot profit from practices that endanger young people without consequence,” Torrez said in a statement Thursday.
“Today’s decision is a victory for every parent who has worried about what social media is doing to their child and every child who deserves to grow up safer online.”
Around three-quarters of the new $567 million fund should be used for mental health treatment, and it’s to be paid over five years.
The remaining amount is allocated across programs for “awareness and prevention,” “screening and assessment,” “referral, linkage, and coordination,” and implementation and evaluation.
Following the ruling, Meta said the company remains “confident in our record of protecting teens online and will continue to defend ourselves against claims that misrepresent the facts.”
Meta will also be required to provide the court with updates twice a year regarding its efforts to comply.
Additionally, the ruling orders Meta to make changes to its products, including making continued efforts to keep children in New Mexico who are under the age of 13 off of Facebook and Instagram.
Age verification for social media users is becoming increasingly popular by regulators around the world, though implementing such policies has proven complex and difficult.
In his ruling, New Mexico Judge Bryan Biedscheid also noted that teenagers are particularly susceptible to features that are designed to boost engagement such as autoplay, infinite scrolling, like counts, push notifications and algorithmic recommendations.
Some of these design features involve industry-wide problems and free speech issues, the ruling says.
However, the judge ordered Meta limit push notifications and usage to 90 hours a month, around three-hours daily on average, for users under age 18, in addition to hiding “like counts.”
Thousands of lawsuits have been filed in the US seeking to hold social media companies liable for alleged harms to children and mental health.
More than 30 US states are suing Meta over similar allegations, with a potential trial set to begin in August in Oakland, California.
In July, a US teenager dropped his lawsuit against Meta just days before the trial was set to begin; the teenager also reached confidential settlements with YouTube, TikTok and Snap.
That case was considered a bellwether that could have set the tone for resolving thousands of similar lawsuits across the country.
The first bellwether trial for social media harms on mental health concluded in March, when a Los Angeles jury ordered Meta and Google to pay a 20-year-old woman $6 million.
In May, Meta, Snap, TikTok and YouTube reached confidential settlements with a Kentucky school district.

item.title: Script search delays 'Bhool Bhulaiyaa'
item.description:
Director Anees Bazmee has said work on “Bhool Bhulaiyaa 4” has been delayed because the team is still searching for the right script, despite reports that the film is in development.
Speaking to Variety India, Bazmee said the challenge is not casting or scheduling but finding a story that can live up to the franchise’s previous installments.
He said: “We put everything in the first three films. We even made the hero Manjulika! So naturally, now we need a great story to make the fourth film.”
Bazmee added that the team is still looking for the right idea and said he would be happy to direct the film once a suitable script is ready.
The filmmaker also praised Kartik Aaryan, who played Rooh Baba in the franchise’s recent installments.
Bazmee said: “I have a great rapport with Kartik. We are good friends, and both the films that we have made turned out to be big hits.”
He described Kartik as a “director’s actor” and added: “His biggest plus point is that he puts in a lot of hard work. If he gets the help of a good director, he can do wonders. He is great at comedy and is full of laughter all day.”
Bazmee said he enjoys working repeatedly with actors with whom he has built a strong professional relationship, citing his collaborations with Ajay Devgn, Akshay Kumar, and Salman Khan.
He said: “I feel it is friendship that when we work with each other, we enjoy it and the whole emotion is different. So, I am sure, with Kartik too, whenever I make a film, we will make a good one.”
While “Bhool Bhulaiyaa 4” remains on hold, Bazmee said he is working to complete a new comedy starring Akshay Kumar, alongside Vidya Balan, Rashii Khanna, and others.

item.title: ‘Dorothy’ teaser offers first look at Karthik Subbaraj’s new film
item.description:
Director Karthik Subbaraj has released the first teaser for his upcoming period drama “Dorothy,” offering a glimpse of a story centered on friendship, conflict, and loss.
The teaser introduces Karthi and Subbu as close friends whose relationship appears to change with the arrival of Keerthy Suresh’s character, Dorothy. Without revealing major plot details, it hints at an emotional conflict between the trio.
Set against a period backdrop, the teaser relies on visuals and music to establish its tone rather than dialogue. Ilaiyaraaja composed the film’s soundtrack.
Sharing the teaser on X, Keerthy Suresh wrote: “Some journeys begin long before the road. Some calls can never be made. And some bonds are tested by a world determined to tear them apart. This is not just a story of friendship. It’s a story of everything that stands in its way.”
Subbaraj announced the film’s title a day before releasing the teaser. He also confirmed that “Dorothy” will have its world premiere at the Toronto International Film Festival (TIFF) before its theatrical release on September 25.
The film is produced by Karthik Subbaraj under Dhammam Films, alongside Guneet Monga and Achin Jain of Sikhya Entertainment. Jyoti Deshpande is producing on behalf of Jio Studios.
The technical team includes S Thirunavukkarasu as cinematographer, Ganesh Siva as editor, Kumar Gangappan as production designer, Dinesh Subbarayan as action choreographer, and Ilaiyaraaja as music composer.

India doesn’t endorse Hasina’s comments: Jaiswal
item.description:
The Government of India does not endorse anything said by Bangladesh's ousted and convicted former prime minister Sheikh Hasina during a press conference held in New Delhi.

Indian Ministry of External Affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal made the remarks on Friday while responding to questions at the ministry's weekly media briefing in New Delhi.

He said, "The Government (of India) does not endorse anything said at the forum, especially with regard to the duly constituted Government of Bangladesh."

Bangladesh outraged as India allows Sheikh Hasina to address press in Delhi: Foreign Ministry

Sheikh Hasina, who has been sentenced to death in connection with crimes against humanity committed during the July uprising and remains a fugitive, joined a press conference via audio call on Wednesday evening. The event was organised by the Foreign Correspondents' Club South Asia (FCC South Asia) in New Delhi.

Before the event, the Bangladesh government had formally conveyed its objection to India. It had also warned that allowing Sheikh Hasina to engage in political activities from Indian soil could hinder efforts to normalise bilateral relations.

Responding to the objection, India's Ministry of External Affairs had said the Government of India had no connection with the event.

Sheikh Hasina's event: Jaiswal says India has no connection

Despite Bangladesh's objection, the programme went ahead. Hasina joined via audio call, delivered a statement and also answered several questions from journalists. Later that night, the Bangladesh government issued a strong reaction.

In a statement, Bangladesh's Ministry of Foreign Affairs said, "Bangladesh is outraged that the absconding convicted genocider Sheikh Hasina was allowed this evening to engage in live interaction with the media in New Delhi where she and her henchmen launched venomous vitriol against the State of Bangladesh and her people."

The ministry's statement also said that Hasina's interaction with journalists from Indian soil on the second anniversary of the July mass uprising was an affront to Bangladesh's sovereignty and a grave insult to those martyred during the uprising.

What analysts say on Hasina’s Delhi press conference and declaration to return home

On Thursday, State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam told journalists that the incident had raised concerns about the future of Bangladesh-India relations.

At Friday's briefing, journalists raised several questions on the issue. In response, Jaiswal said, "I have already stated government's position on the issue before the press conference happened. You would have seen those remarks, you were present here. I am reiterating it here: Government had no role to play in what was an event by a private media entity, and government does not endorse anything said at the forum, especially with regard to the duly constituted government of Bangladesh.”

Jaiswal had made essentially the same remarks in response to questions on the previous day.

Allowing Sheikh Hasina to speak in Delhi to the media is disrespectful to Bangladesh

However, on Friday he added that, "especially with regard to the duly constituted Government of Bangladesh." He said, “The government (of India) has no involvement whatsoever in it and does not endorse any views that may be expressed at the forum,” He repeated the same point in Hindi after making it in English.

During the New Delhi event, Sajeeb Wazed, who joined virtually from the United States, said Bangladesh was rapidly turning into another Pakistan. Referring to that remark at Friday's briefing, a journalist asked whether India endorsed the allegation and how concerned it was about the situation in Bangladesh.

In response, Jaiswal said, “We keep a close watch on all the developments in our neighbourhood. India pays particular attention to its national security and takes appropriate steps in response to any development or situation."

Jaiswal did not comment on whether India endorsed or rejected Sajeeb Wazed's allegation.

item.description:
A Biman Bangladesh Airlines flight from Toronto to Dhaka made an emergency landing at Rome’s Fiumicino Airport due to a technical issue and remained grounded there for at least six hours, officials said.
A public relations official of Biman Bangladesh Airlines confirmed the development on Friday evening, saying the aircraft was grounded after undergoing technical inspections following the emergency landing.
“The aircraft underwent a technical check after landing. Following an initial inspection, the authorities declared it grounded,” the official said, requesting anonymity.
Around 250 passengers were on board the flight.
The national flag carrier is working to arrange alternative flights, accommodation and meals for the affected passengers, the official added.

Tuku: Newspaper is the main driving force of any country
item.description:
State Minister for Fisheries and Livestock Sultan Salahuddin Tuku on Friday said that newspapers are one of the main driving forces of any country, playing a vital role in guiding society and highlighting its problems.
Speaking at the publication ceremony of the newly launched weekly ‘Somoy Torongo’ in Tangail, the state minister said the media helps expose various social irregularities and corruption, while also providing direction so that people can move forward and society can function in an orderly and democratic manner.
"However, there is also irresponsible journalism. Such practices must be avoided," he said. "A newspaper is one of the principal driving forces of a nation, helping steer the country in the right direction."
Addressing the gathering, Tuku said Tangail is a large and prosperous district with many achievements to its credit. "There is much to be proud of in Tangail. To move the district forward, people from all professions must work together in unity. Everyone must abide by the rules," he said.
He also emphasized the government's commitment to democratic values, saying, "We will never obstruct the democratic process. We will not interfere with anyone's freedom. We will extend our fullest cooperation to journalists, who will independently choose their own leadership."
Chaired by Roshan Ali, Editor and Publisher of the weekly Somoy Torongo, the program was also attended by Hasanuzzaman Shahin, President of Tangail District BNP, Mahmudul Haque Sanu, former Member Secretary, Azgar Ali, President of Sadar Upazila BNP, Jafar Ahmed, Secretary General of the Bangladesh Regional Newspapers Council, Kazi Zakirul Molla, General Secretary of the Tangail Press Club, and Mamunur Rahman, President of the Tangail Television Reporters Forum.
The program was conducted by journalist Malek Adnan. Prominent social and cultural personalities, journalists, and people from various professions were also present at the event.

item.title: Content creator Ripon Mia arrested in Netrokona schoolgirl rape case
item.description:
The Rapid Action Battalion (RAB) on Friday arrested content creator Ripon Mia, 33, the prime accused in a rape case involving a 14-year-old schoolgirl in Netrokona Sadar Upazila.
He was arrested during a raid in the Mohisharan-Achintyapur area of Gouripur Upazila in Mymensingh on Friday morning, according to a RAB-14 press release issued in the afternoon.
According to a RAB-14 press release issued on Friday afternoon, a team from the elite force's Headquarters Company arrested fugitive accused Ripon Mia during a raid conducted on a tip-off. He was later handed over to Netrokona Model Police Station.
According to the case statement and police, Ripon had allegedly harassed the victim on several occasions under the pretext of making videos. At around 8:00pm on July 30, he allegedly went to the girl's house, told her he had an urgent matter to discuss, took her to the northern bank of the Mogra River and raped her.
After the incident came to light, a local arbitration (salish) was held at a BNP party office in a nearby market on Monday night, where locals decided to fine Ripon Tk500,000 and oust him from the village.
Ripon was given one week to pay the fine and leave the village. The incident drew widespread attention after videos of the arbitration were circulated on social media. The victim's father later filed a rape case with Netrokona Model Police Station on Tuesday night.
Several videos of the arbitration have since gone viral on Facebook. In one 30-second clip, Ripon appears to admit to the allegation and apologises to those present. At one point, he says, "Whether I made a mistake or not, I did. I have to live among you all. People make mistakes, and I made one."
Officer-in-Charge (OC) Abul Khayer of Netrokona Model Police Station said Ripon had been produced before the court.
Ripon, a resident of a village in Netrokona Sadar Upazila, works as a carpenter. He rose to prominence by creating videos on social media from 2016 and now has nearly 1.9 million followers on a Facebook page launched in 2019.

item.title: Anne: Govt plans to re-excavate 20,000 km canal nationwide
item.description:
The government plans to re-excavate at least 20,000 kilometres of canals across Bangladesh as part of an initiative to improve water management, agriculture and environmental sustainability, Water Resources Minister Shahiduddin Chowdhury Anne said on Friday.
As part of the programme, he said, the Ministry of Water Resources will soon send a special technical team to Jahangirnagar University (JU) to conduct surveys and prepare for the re-excavation of canals on the campus.
The minister made the remarks while addressing a doa and discussion meeting organised by Jahangirnagar University, marking the second anniversary of the July Uprising.
"The university's teachers and the vice-chancellor requested the re-excavation of canals. The matter has already been forwarded to the ministry secretary. A special technical team will soon visit the university to conduct the necessary survey and technical assessment," Anne said.
He added that following the assessment, the canal re-excavation project at JU would be implemented with funding from the Ministry of Water Resources. Necessary steps would also be taken to restore the university's lakes, he said.
He said the initiative is expected to boost agricultural production, improve irrigation, restore ecological balance, enhance inland water transport, create employment opportunities and help replenish declining groundwater levels.
Speaking at the event, JU Vice-Chancellor Prof Mohammad Kamrul Ahsan said people from different backgrounds had stood together during the July movement, but many were now facing difficulties due to what he described as "petty politics."
"We need to move away from this political culture," he said.
The program, chaired by the vice-chancellor, was attended by Pro-Vice Chancellor (Administration) Prof Md Nazrul Islam, Pro-Vice Chancellor (Education) Prof Shamsul Alam, Proctor Prof Zakir Hossain, teachers, and leaders and activists of the Bangladesh Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal, among others.

item.title: Gold worth Tk 38 lakh looted in Gazipur
item.description:
An armed gang of robbers looted 17 bhoris of gold jewelry worth an estimated Tk 38 lakh, Tk 100,000 in cash, a smartphone, and other valuables from a house in Sreepur upazila of Gazipur early on Friday.
The robbery occurred around 2:00 am in Panchultia (Molla Bari) village under Goshinga Union. According to the victims, four masked robbers forced their way into the house after breaking down the main door with a heavy wooden beam.
Armed with machetes and knives, they held homeowner Abdus Samad Molla and his wife, Suraiya Begum, at knifepoint while searching the house.
Suraiya Begum said the robbers threatened to abduct the couple’s grandchildren if they failed to hand over their valuables, forcing the family to comply.
Abdus Samad Molla said his three daughters had been staying at the house for two days to attend a nearby wedding. As their husbands, along with one of his sons, work in Saudi Arabia, the daughters had stored their jewelry and savings at the family home.
The stolen items included seven bhoris of gold belonging to one daughter, another seven bhoris owned by a second daughter, and three bhoris belonging to the youngest daughter, in addition to cash and a smartphone.
Sreepur Police Station Officer-in-Charge Mohammad Shahinur Alam said that they inspected the house, spoke with family members, and were collecting evidence. He said legal proceedings were underway and efforts had begun to identify and arrest those involved.

item.title: Prolonged delay in road repair work triggers 15-km tailback in Comilla
item.description:
Continuous delays in repairing roads riddled with potholes caused by torrential rainfall have triggered a tailback stretching 15 kilometres on the Dhaka-Chittagong highway, causing severe suffering to thousands of passengers and transport workers.
The congestion began early Friday from the Mainamati area and stretched to Suagazi in Sadar south upazila, with long queues of vehicles seen on both lanes.
Anisur Rahman (SI), Mainamati Highway Crossing Police Station, said vehicles were moving slowly due to repair work, although the congestion was not permanent.
Almas Khan, a businessman returning to Dhaka from Feni, said he got stuck in traffic at Paduar Bazar around noon and took two and a half hours to reach Mainamati. Several ambulances carrying patients were also seen stuck in the congestion.
A police report said rainwater had created large potholes near Amtali, close to Comilla Cantonment, forcing Dhaka-bound vehicles to move slowly. Some vehicles attempted to drive on the wrong side, affecting the Chittagong-bound lane as well.
Police deployed two mobile teams and additional personnel at key points to control the situation.
Kirtiman Chakma (ASP), Highway Police Comilla Region, said continuous rain over the past three to four weeks had severely damaged the road. At least four cargo trucks became stuck in potholes over the past two days, causing prolonged disruptions while being removed by tow trucks.

item.title: Biman flight makes emergency landing in Rome
item.description:
A Biman Bangladesh Airlines flight from Toronto to Dhaka made an emergency landing at Rome’s Fiumicino Airport due to a technical issue and remained grounded there for at least six hours, officials said.
A public relations official of Biman Bangladesh Airlines confirmed the development on Friday evening, saying the aircraft was grounded after undergoing technical inspections following the emergency landing.
“The aircraft underwent a technical check after landing. Following an initial inspection, the authorities declared it grounded,” the official said, requesting anonymity.
Around 250 passengers were on board the flight.
The national flag carrier is working to arrange alternative flights, accommodation and meals for the affected passengers, the official added.

item.title: Swapon: July uprising opens historic opportunity to institutionalise democracy
item.description:
Information and Broadcasting Minister Zahir Uddin Swapon on Friday said the historic July Uprising has created an unprecedented opportunity to establish and institutionalize true democratic values and structures in the country.
"A rare opportunity has emerged in Bangladesh today to structurally shape and institutionalize democratic values through a series of transformations—uprising, sacrifices, a spontaneous election, government formation, and an active parliament," he said.
The minister made the remarks while addressing as the chief guest a discussion titled "July Uprising and Bangladesh's Democratic Transition," organized by the Dhaka University Debating Society (DUDS) at the Teacher-Student Centre (TSC) of the university Friday evening.
Swapon urged all democratic forces and the young generation to embrace the deep responsibility bestowed by the martyrs of the July movement, warning against self-complacency, stardom-seeking mindsets on digital platforms, or attempts to monopolize the credit of a popular revolution.
"The martyrs have drawn a roadmap for our future with their lives. To walk that path, we must overcome frivolity and frivolous tendencies. Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has rightly stated that the sole credit for this triumph belongs to the people, the people, and the people," he added.
Reaffirming the government's commitment to building an effective parliamentary system, the information minister noted that a functional parliament is the main core for narrowing down non-democratic practices.
He expressed optimism that all pro-democracy allies would utilize the parliamentary platform rather than reverting to street-level misgivings.
Highlighting the historic continuity of Bangladesh's struggle for dignity, equality, and rights, Swapon stressed that the spirit of the 1971 War of Liberation, the 1990 anti-autocracy movement, and the July Uprising are interconnected chapters of the nation's democratic evolution.
"If anyone thinks that history begins only from now and tries to erase the past, they will fail to understand the complete Bangladesh. To comprehend the full canvas of Bangladesh, one must understand both our thousand-year history and the nation defined by its red and green flag," he said.

item.title: Gas shortage intensifies load shedding in Chittagong
item.description:
The partial resumption of operations at the floating LNG terminal in Moheshkhali of Cox’s Bazar has brought only limited relief to Chittagong, where a prolonged gas shortage continues to disrupt electricity generation and worsen daily load shedding across the region.
The LNG terminal resumed operations after remaining shut for nearly two weeks because of a technical fault. However, the restoration has not been sufficient to meet the region's energy demand.
As a result, households and businesses in Chittagong experience frequent power outages, with many residents reporting five to six hours of load shedding every day. Rural communities are facing even longer interruptions.
According to the Bangladesh Power Development Board (BPDB), Chittagong has 28 power plants powered by gas, furnace oil, coal and hydropower. Six of those plants were out of operation on August 3 due to mechanical problems, fuel shortages or scheduled operating patterns.
Although the region's installed generation capacity exceeds 4,600 megawatts, actual production has dropped significantly because gas-fired plants are unable to operate at full capacity.
Official data show that electricity generation reached 2,819.14 MW during off-peak hours and 3,302.60 MW during peak hours on August 3. The BPDB reported electricity demand of 1,352.96 MW during off-peak hours and 1,477.2 MW during peak hours, with load shedding recorded at 65 MW and 62 MW respectively.
Consumers, however, said that the official figures do not reflect the reality on the ground, adding that power cuts have become much more frequent and prolonged.
Residents across the city say repeated outages have disrupted daily life and damaged electrical appliances due to constant voltage fluctuations. In rural parts of Chittagong, some areas are experiencing six to seven hours of power cuts each day, making living conditions increasingly difficult during the hot summer months.
The gas shortage has also forced major government-owned power plants to reduce output. Two 210 MW units at the Raozan power station, with a combined capacity of 420 MW, have remained shut because of inadequate gas supply.
The 225 MW Shikalbaha gas-fired power plant has also scaled back production. Plant officials said full-capacity operation requires about 37 million cubic feet of gas per day, but the facility has recently been receiving only 28 to 30 million cubic feet, limiting electricity generation to around 183-184 MW.
According to Karnaphuli Gas Distribution Company Limited (KGDCL), Chittagong's daily gas demand stands at approximately 350 million cubic feet, while current supply is only 200-220 million cubic feet, leaving a daily shortfall of up to 150 million cubic feet. The deficit has affected residential, commercial and transport sectors in addition to electricity generation.
KGDCL Managing Director Engineer Md Salahuddin said that it will take several more days before gas supply returns to normal.
RPGCL Manager Imtiaz Kamal Chowdhury said one terminal has resumed supplying around 180 million cubic feet of gas per day alongside another terminal supplying about 570 million cubic feet.
Following repairs carried out with the assistance of foreign specialists, gas transmission has resumed gradually. However, authorities acknowledge that restoring full electricity generation and stabilising power supply across the region will take additional time.

Forest official secretly leaves post after promising to return bribe money
item.description:
A forest department official posted at Maudubi Union in Rangabali upazila of Patuakhali allegedly left his workplace secretly after taking bribes in exchange for issuing permits required for fishing in rivers connected to the Bay of Bengal.

The acting beat officer, Soyeb Khan, had promised the alleged victims that he would return their money before leaving his post. Prothom Alo obtained an audio recording related to the matter.

In a 20-minute and 24-second audio clip, the accused official can be heard talking with several alleged victims. Jahir Uddin, the official who had recently joined the same post, was also present during the conversation.

At one point in the recording, Soyeb Khan is heard saying, "Both parties paid money for the char. Whoever I cannot allocate the char to, I will return their money before I leave. If someone does not want to take the money back, what can I do? I will return everyone's money. I will not keep a single penny belonging to anyone. I will settle everyone's issue before I leave."

Victim fisherman Ilias Patowari said he had paid Tk 100,000 after being promised a fishing permit for a designated area. As he did not receive the permit as agreed, he and several others went to the accused official's office on the night of 22 July to demand their money back. During the meeting, he secretly recorded the conversation about the financial transactions on his mobile phone.

Jahir Uddin, who replaced Soyeb Khan, told Prothom Alo that after joining, he discussed Soyeb Khan's financial dealings with several local residents. He said Soyeb Khan left the workplace without properly handing over his responsibilities.

Jahir said he did not know exactly when Soyeb Khan left. Since then, many people have been contacting him regularly in the hope of recovering their money.

According to the Forest Department and the alleged victims, owners of boats and trawlers operating in areas adjacent to the Bay of Bengal are required to obtain clearance from the local forest office to fish in those waters.

Government rules stipulate a revenue fee of Tk 575 for obtaining a fishing permit for an engine-run trawler measuring 50 feet in length, 6 feet in width, 4 to 6 feet in depth and having a carrying capacity of 520 maunds, using a khorchi net.

However, the accused official allegedly collected between Tk 25,000 and Tk 400,000 per person by promising to issue permits for fishing in rivers and canals and for collecting grass from chars as cattle feed.

Tanbin Biswas, president of the Maudubi Union unit of Jatiyatabadi Swechchhasebak Dal, alleged that Soyeb Khan took Tk 86,000 from him after promising to issue a permit but never provided one.

Later, when the official repeatedly delayed returning the money, Tanbin recorded a video of his confession.

On 25 July, he received Tk 40,000 back through Rangabali upazila Jubo Dal Member Secretary Niaz Akon. At least 30 local people have made similar allegations of paying money.

Local union parishad member Md Mohasin Uddin Bhuiya also alleged that Tk 100,000 had been taken from him. He said that when Range Officer Amir Hossain, who joined Rangabali on 23 July, visited the area, he and other alleged victims submitted their complaints.

He claimed that the range officer wrote down the names of the complainants and the amounts they were owed on a piece of paper and took their signatures.

Speaking to Prothom Alo over the phone, the accused forest official, Soyeb Khan, said, "Unnecessary allegations are being made because I have been transferred. However, I have resolved most of the issues."

He later said he would provide further details via WhatsApp before disconnecting the call. Despite several subsequent attempts, he did not respond.

Contacted for comment, Rangabali Range Officer Amir Hossain said, "I joined Rangabali on 22 July. The following day, when I visited the Maudubi area, local people verbally accused Soyeb Khan of taking bribes. However, I did not take anyone's signature on a paper mentioning the names of the alleged victims or the amounts involved."

Repeated attempts to contact Patuakhali Divisional Forest Officer Md Jahidur Rahman Mia by mobile phone for comment went unanswered.
